description: Own-wording mouth hints for the dot-toggle tile. DRAFT, not checked by a speech teacher or native speaker. The sounds themselves are read from consonants.json at runtime (single source). Pairs: bet/vet, kaf/khaf, pe/fe (dagesh) and shin/sin (dot position).

hints.with: Both lips press together and pop open.
hints.without: Top teeth touch the lower lip; air buzzes through.

hints.with: The back of the tongue blocks the air for a moment, then releases.
hints.without: The back of the tongue leaves a narrow gap and air rubs through, like a rough h from the throat.

hints.with: Both lips press together and pop open, with no buzz.
hints.without: Top teeth touch the lower lip; air rushes through, no buzz.

hints.with: Right-hand dot (shin): tongue pulled back a little, a hushing sound.
hints.without: Left-hand dot (sin): tongue tip near the teeth, a hissing s sound.

caveats: Which form a word uses (dotted or not) depends on the letter's position and the vowel before it. This tile only teaches what the dot does; it does not decide which form a given word has.
A dagesh also appears in other letters, where it does not change the sound audibly in Israeli Hebrew. Only bet, kaf and pe change sound.
Sephardi bet is sometimes described as softer than [b]; the data marks this as declining and unverified. The tile shows the Israeli textbook contrast.
